subject: Harmattan is here. Is your voice ready?
preview_text: This week I wrote about dry air, cooling your voice down and wrong notes.
body:
Hi {{ subscriber.first_name | default: "friend" }},

The dry season has started, and for a lot of singers that means a croaky first line on Sunday morning. Three of my new posts are about keeping your voice working through the dry air and after a long service. The fourth is about what your face does when a note goes wrong.

Your voice in harmattan: the croak was booked on Saturday
If your voice comes out rough on Sunday morning, the trouble usually started the night before. Here is my Saturday-to-Sunday plan, and why a bottle of water only fixes half of it.
https://blog.joshuaediale.com/posts/harmattan-voice-sunday-plan/

Your voice was only built for Warri… and these are the consequences
My voice started cracking when I moved from Warri to Abuja. If you have moved somewhere drier, or you sing under freezing AC, the checklist at the end is for you.
https://blog.joshuaediale.com/posts/voice-built-for-warri/

Your voice needs a slow landing after Sunday
You warm up before you sing, but do you cool down after? The cool-down takes 4 minutes, and I show you how to tell if it is working.
https://blog.joshuaediale.com/posts/your-voice-needs-a-slow-landing/

Your face is the second mistake
Sooner or later a wrong note will come, from you or from the band. What you do in the 2 seconds after it matters, and you can practise for it.
https://blog.joshuaediale.com/posts/your-face-is-the-second-mistake/

{{ subscriber.first_name | default: "friend" }}, if your Sunday service runs long, start with the slow landing post. By the benediction your voice has worked hard, so give it a slow landing.

What does your voice feel like on a dry Sunday morning? Reply and tell me.

Joshua Ediale
MusicMentor by Joshua Ediale
